title: GPU workload classifier and SLA tagging guidelines
author: Jordan Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: Provide a consistent classification and tagging scheme for GPU workloads across Redwood Inference so that scheduler, billing, and SRE tooling can make deterministic decisions about placement, preemption tolerance, and SLA enforcement. This document defines the taxonomy, tag conventions, enforcement patterns (Terraform + CI gates), and operational runbooks for common mis-tagging and quota scenarios.

Scope: Applies to all internal and customer-facing GPU workloads running on Hosted, Dedicated, and Private clusters. Excludes ephemeral CI CPU-only jobs (see CI/CD playground policies).

Goals
- Enable automated placement decisions (warm pool vs. spot vs. reserved) by exposing workload intent via tags.
- Make SLAs machine-readable for routing, preemptibility, and cost accounting.
- Reduce incidents caused by misconfiguration (e.g., production traffic scheduled on preemptible nodes).
- Provide a clear rollback and remediation runbook for tag-related incidents.

Tagging taxonomy
We standardize a set of tags attached to job/tenant metadata and Terraform resource labels. Tags must be present on cluster attachments, pod templates, and tenant manifests. All tags are lowercase, dash-separated.

Tag schema table
| tag | description | allowed values / format | owner |
|-----|-------------|------------------------:|-------|
| env | workload environment | prod | staging | dev | product (string) | SRE / platform |
| sla.priority | routing and placement priority | platinum | gold | silver | bronze | product / infra |
| sla.latency | expected 95th percentile token latency | <milliseconds, e.g. 150ms> | infra |
| preemptible | preemption tolerance | true | false | infra |
| workload.class | coarse workload class | realtime-inference | batch-eval | training | background | product |
| cost.center | billing cost center id | CC-xxxxx | finance |

Example tag set (string representation):
- env=prod
- sla.priority=gold
- sla.latency=120ms
- preemptible=false
- workload.class=realtime-inference
- cost.center=CC-02142

SLA mapping and enforced behaviors
- platinum: guaranteed capacity in Dedicated pools, sla.latency <= 50ms p95, preemptible=false, rollback to compatible low-memory variant if perf regression > 20% within 10m.
- gold: routed to warm pools or reserved burst; sla.latency <= 150ms p95; preemptible=false preferred but can be true with explicit approval.
- silver: allowed on heterogeneous or preemptible-backed pools; sla.latency <= 500ms p95; preemptible=true allowed.
- bronze: background and low-priority batch work, preemptible=true mandatory for cost control.

Enforcement patterns
1) Terraform module validation (pre-commit/CI):
   - A policy-as-code check that validates required tags exist for every gpu_node_group and tenant module. Missing tags fail plan stage.
   - Integrate with OPA/rego gate in the repo: repo: infra/tenant-modules -> pre-merge gate.

2) Admission webhook in clusters:
   - kube-metadata-admitter validates pod labels and rejects pods that run GPUs without env and sla.priority tags.

3) Runtime auditing:
   - nightly job (gpu-tag-auditor) that emits violations to metrics (counter: gpu_tag_violations_total) and opens tickets when high-cost mis-tagging detected.

Terraform snippet (example enforcement variable and tag usage)
```
module "tenant_gpu" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@redwood/repo.git//modules/tenant-gpu?ref=v1.4"
  tenant_id = var.tenant_id
  tags = {
    env            = var.env
    sla_priority   = var.sla_priority
    workload_class = var.workload_class
    cost_center    = var.cost_center
  }
}
```

Admission policy example (Rego pseudo-rule)
```
package admission.gpu

deny[msg] {
  input.request.object.spec.gpu_count > 0
  not input.request.object.metadata.labels.env
  msg = "GPU pod missing env label"
}
```

Classifier rules (yaml example used by scheduler):
```
- match:
    labels:
      workload.class: realtime-inference
  route:
    pool: warm-reserved
    preemptible: false
- match:
    labels:
      workload.class: batch-eval
  route:
    pool: spot-burst
    preemptible: true
```

Operational runbooks
1) Incident: Production traffic scheduled on preemptible nodes
   Indicators:
   - Elevated p95 token latency for prod tenants
   - Alert: node_eviction_rate > 0.5% and pods with env=prod and preemptible=true present
   Triage steps:
   1. Oncall pulls last 30m of allocation events: `kubectl get pods -l env=prod -o wide` and cross references node labels.
   2. If pods are on preemptible nodes, check Terraform plan history: `git log -S"preemptible=true" infra/tenant-modules` to identify recent changes.
   3. Remediate: If mis-tagged, patch workload labels: `kubectl label pod <pod> preemptible=false --overwrite` and trigger a rolling restart of the deployment.
   4. If the issue is widespread, escalate to infra@redwood and trigger warm-pool scale-up policy: `./tools/warm-pool-scale --tenant $TENANT --factor 1.5`
   5. Open a post-incident ticket and set required fix: update the Terraform module to include explicit tag validation and add unit tests in the module's test harness (owner: tenant-iac-team).

2) Incident: Missing mandatory tags detected in nightly audit
   Triage steps:
   1. gpu-tag-auditor will create a jira with list of resources. The SRE triage lead assigns to tenant owner.
   2. If owner is unknown, use cost.center to map via finance ledger and notify cost center owner.
   3. Fix: apply tag patch through terraform import + `terraform apply` or for ephemeral CI jobs, update pipeline variables to append required tags.

Rollout plan for enforcement changes
- Week 0: Soft audit only – nightly auditor creates tickets but does not block deploys.
- Week 2: CI fails on missing tags for new merges (enables rewrite for contributors).
- Week 4: Admission webhook enabled in staging clusters.
- Week 6: Admission webhook enabled in prod for non-critical namespaces.
- Week 8: Full enforcement in prod namespaces; auto-remediation playbooks enabled.

Observability and metrics to monitor
- gpu_tag_violations_total (counter) – goal < 5/week
- gpu_pod_misplacement_ratio (gauge) – p95 < 0.5%
- sla_latency_p95_by_tenant (histogram) – alert when above mapped sla.latency for more than 5m
- cost_center_gpu_spend_by_sla (timeseries) – used for monthly chargeback and anomaly detection

Ownership and contacts
- Policy owner: Platform / infra (owner alias: infra-platform@redwood)
- Oncall: SRE rotation (see /eng-infra/eng-sre/oncall-rotations for roster)
- Terraform module owner: tenant-iac-team (leads: Maya Chen, Rafael Ortiz)
- CI gate maintainers: CI/CD team (lead: Priya Nair)

Testing guidance
- Unit tests: module-level unit tests for tag generation (use terratest) are required for all changes.
- Integration: run admission webhook against a local kind cluster in CI.
- Chaos: include one scheduled experiment per quarter where a small set of prod-like tenants are intentionally mis-tagged and the auditor/alerting paths are validated.

Frequently asked questions
- Q: What if a tenant needs low-latency but also wants to use spot instances?
  A: Use sla.priority=gold and set a preemptible flag with an approved exception. The scheduler will attempt warm-reserved and fallback to compatible quantized models if preemption occurs.

- Q: How do we onboard a new cost center?
  A: Create an entry in finance ledger, then update the tenant onboarding Terraform module with cost_center value. The onboarding runbook will validate tags as part of the CI pipeline.

Appendices
- Commonly referenced automation: `gpu-tag-auditor`, `gpu-classifier`, `warm-pool-scale` (internal tools in infra/tools).
- Related pages: see page links in metadata for quota and fair-share patterns.

Change log
